newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AGA sees '96 result 15 pct lower than '95.
newsitem.headline: AGA sees '96 result 15 pct lower than '95.

text.p: Swedish gas company AGA on Monday posted a 14 percent drop in nine-month profit after financial items and said its result for the full year was likely to be at least 15 percent lower than 1995.
"(This is) due primarily to a continued weak economic climate in several countries and the stronger Swedish crown," AGA said in its nine-month report.

AGA reported a pre-tax profit after financial items but before capital gains of 1.38 billion crowns for the nine months ending September 30, compared with the 1.60 billion reported for the same 1995 period.
Of the fourteen percent earnings drop, six percentage points were due to the stronger Swedish currency during the year, AGA said.
Sales for the period fell by five percent to 9.52 billion crowns, but the company said invoicing had increased by three percent discounting the effects of the stronger crown.
The increased scope of AGA's capital expenditure programme had led to higher depreciation in relation to sales, the company said.

"An increased focus on product development in the parent company, initial costs of rationalisation programmes in several companies, and temporarily high costs for product supply in some markets also contributed to the decline in earnings," it said.

Investments over the period totalled 2.06 billion crowns, with major projects including air separation plants under construction in Sweden, Norway, Russia, the Netherlands, France, Austria, Brazil, Columbia and Argentina.
AGA's president Magnus Storch struck a disappointed tone as he commented on the group's results for the last time as company chief executive.
"I have to note that the result for the third quarter also failed to meet our expectations...1996 will therefore not be such a good year for AGA in terms of results," Storch said.
